name: claude-code-usage-tracker
description: Real-time monitoring of Claude Code token usage, cost tracking, and session management

claude-usage-monitor.configDir.markdownDescription:
Which Claude Code config directory this window reports on — the equivalent of `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, for people running more than one account. `~` is expanded.

Example: `~/.claude-work`.

Leave empty to use `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, then `~/.claude`. Note that setting `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` through `claudeCode.environmentVariables` or `terminal.integrated.env.*` does **not** reach this extension — those only inject into the Claude Code process and integrated terminals respectively — so this setting is the way to do it per window.

Cached usage, burn-rate history and notification state are namespaced per directory, so two windows on two accounts stay independent.

claude-usage-monitor.clockFormat.description: Clock format for reset times in the usage panel.

claude-usage-monitor.statusBarFormat.markdownDescription:
Template for the status bar text. Windows are addressed as `{5h.…}`, `{7d.…}`, `{extra.…}` (pay-as-you-go), `{max.…}` (whichever is highest right now) or `{model:<display name>.…}` (e.g. `{model:Fable.pct}`). Fields: `.pct`, `.reset`, `.resetAt`, `.name`, `.bar`, plus `.spent` and `.limit` on the pay-as-you-go window. `{icon}` inserts the Claude mark, `{{`/`}}` escape braces, and a token for a window your account does not report renders empty.

Examples:
- `{icon} {5h.pct} · {5h.reset}` → `12% · 3h 40m`
- `{icon} {max.name} {max.pct}` → follows whichever window is worst
- `{icon} {extra.spent} / {extra.limit}` → `$12.50 / $40.00`

Leave empty to follow `#claude-usage-monitor.statusBar#`. The usage panel's Settings tab has presets and a live preview.

claude-usage-monitor.statusBar.markdownDescription: Which quota window to show in the status bar text: `5h`, `7d`, `both`, or `model:<display name>`. Superseded by `#claude-usage-monitor.statusBarFormat#`, which is used instead whenever it is set.

claude-usage-monitor.statusBarColorFrom.markdownDescription:
Which windows drive the status bar background color — it turns orange/red when the highest of them crosses a threshold. Use window addresses: `5h`, `7d`, `model:<display name>`, or `*` for every window the account reports.

Example: `["5h", "7d", "model:Fable"]`.

Legacy string values (`max`, `5h`, `7d`, `model:…`) are still honored.

enumDescriptions: Fill the item with the theme's warning/error background (current behaviour)
Leave the background alone and tint the text instead
Leave the colours alone and append a coloured emoji
No level signal in the status bar at all
claude-usage-monitor.statusBarIndicator.markdownDescription:
How the status bar signals that a quota window has crossed a threshold.

- `background` — the theme's warning/error background. VS Code allows extensions only these two colours and picks the matching text colour itself, so on some themes the contrast is poor.
- `text` — no background; the text is tinted using `#claude-usage-monitor.statusBarColors#`.
- `emoji` — no background; a glyph from `#claude-usage-monitor.statusBarEmoji#` is appended. Readable on every theme, and it still reads for colour-blind and screen-reader users.
- `none` — no signal in the bar; the tooltip, panel and notifications still show the level.

The `{dot}` format token works in every mode, so you can place the emoji yourself — or combine it with a background.

To restyle `background` mode itself, edit VS Code's own tokens — the usage panel's Settings tab has a field and colour picker for each, or by hand: `"workbench.colorCustomizations": { "statusBarItem.warningBackground": "#7A6400", "statusBarItem.warningForeground": "#FFFFFF" }`. Either way that applies to every extension's status bar item, not only this one.

normal.description: Below the warning threshold. Empty leaves the status bar's own colour.

warning.description: At or above the warning threshold.

error.description: At or above the error threshold, and while a window is exhausted.

claude-usage-monitor.statusBarColors.markdownDescription: Text colours for `text` mode of `#claude-usage-monitor.statusBarIndicator#`. Each value is either a theme colour id — `editorWarning.foreground`, `charts.red`, `terminal.ansiYellow` — which follows light/dark themes, or a literal CSS colour such as `#e5c100`. Empty means the status bar's default colour.

normal.description: Below the warning threshold. Empty by default — a permanent green dot is noise.

warning.description: At or above the warning threshold.

error.description: At or above the error threshold, and while a window is exhausted.

claude-usage-monitor.statusBarEmoji.markdownDescription: Glyphs used by `emoji` mode of `#claude-usage-monitor.statusBarIndicator#`, and by the `{dot}` format token in any mode. Any text works, not just emoji. Keep the glyphs the same width or the bar will shift as the level changes — the emoji-presentation shapes (🟢 🟡 🔴 🟠 ⚠️) are all double-width.

claude-usage-monitor.burnRate.markdownDescription:
**Beta.** Keep a short local history of your usage to draw a trend line for each quota window, estimate how fast it is being consumed, and project when it will run out. Treat the projections as a rough guide.

Off by default because it is the only feature that records anything. The history never leaves your machine, is capped at 64 KB (typically ~5 KB), is discarded for each window when that window resets, and is deleted entirely when this is switched off.

enumDescriptions: Notify at the error threshold and when a window is exhausted (default)
Also notify at the warning threshold
claude-usage-monitor.notifications.markdownDescription: Show a notification when a quota window crosses a threshold. Each window notifies at most once per reset cycle, so this never repeats on every poll.

claude-usage-monitor.warningThreshold.description: Utilization percentage at which the status bar turns orange (warning).

claude-usage-monitor.errorThreshold.description: Utilization percentage at which the status bar turns red (error).
